findings.engineBasis: head-chromium/report.json explicitly binds engine=chromium and natural-input/no-state-injection capture flags.
findings.assertion: The isolated native front-fork/tire pivot must be separately player-visible in the natural rear-chase view to close this perceptual branch.
findings.observedPixels: Viewed full-frame current-build PNG: rear-chase rider, lane position and broader body-bank cue are visible, but the fork/tire steering assembly is tiny and partly occluded behind the rider silhouette; the pivot cannot be judged independently.
remainingGaps: No isolated player-visible front-fork/tire pivot is established by this frame. Renderer pose telemetry or the visible lane arc/body bank cannot substitute for that visual evidence.

limitations: The rear-chase camera shows the white head/neck and coral helmet, but the forward-facing orange beak is not exposed consistently; no beak animation or front-facing recognizability claim is inferred.
The standalone native-front-fork pivot remains BLOCKED by the supplied task status and is not closed by head, HUD, pause or route-menu pixels.

Compact route-menu screenshots confirm the selected route and CTA, while lower route rows are partially clipped at the initial scroll position; full scroll interaction was outside this supplemental pixel pass.
Evidence is automated desktop-browser emulation only; physical phone readability, human enjoyment, live ad integration and native platform packages are not evaluated here.
